passage: All morning in Durban Thabo, two, flapped his hands and bounced by the front door. "Beach! Beach!" he squealed, and his father Siddiq caught the feeling and laughed as he packed the bag. At the sand Thabo ran, shrieked and dug. When Siddiq said it was time to go, Thabo's face crumpled and he sobbed, clinging to his bucket all the way to the car.

qa.q: What did Thabo do by the door all morning?
qa.a: He flapped his hands and bounced while calling out "Beach!"

qa.q: What might Thabo's sobbing at the end suggest, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: It suggests the big excitement and the sudden end were hard to handle. He might also have been tired from the day.

qa.q: What could Siddiq do to make endings easier?
qa.a: He can give a warning before leaving, name the feeling, and promise the next visit or a small ritual. 🙂

qa.q: How does Siddiq's laughing affect Thabo's morning?
qa.a: His shared excitement makes Thabo's feeling bigger and more fun, since it spreads between them.

grounding: A toddler flaps hands, bounces and squeals before an outing, excitement is contagious and can turn to tears when it ends.

passage: I am Seema, and from my window I watched Jomon, about two, jump up and down on the pavement when the ice-cream cart bell rang. He flapped both hands and squealed, and his mother laughed with him. Later he licked the cone happily, but when the last bite was gone, he wailed and threw himself against her legs. I cannot tell whether he was sad about the cone or just overtired.

qa.q: What did Jomon do when he heard the ice-cream bell?
qa.a: He jumped up and down, flapped both hands and squealed.

qa.q: What does Jomon's wail after the last bite suggest, and what else might explain it?
qa.a: It suggests the excitement had risen so high that the end felt like a loss. He might also just have been tired.

qa.q: What could Jomon's mother do at that moment?
qa.a: She can hold him, say that the ice cream is finished and that is a sad ending, and offer something else to look at.

qa.q: How might Seema's view differ from the mother's?
qa.a: Seema sees only part of the day from the window, so Seema is guessing, while the mother knows Jomon's mood and routine.

grounding: A toddler flaps hands, bounces and squeals before a treat, and a big build-up can turn to tears when it ends.

passage:
Friday evening: Lakshmi told Omkar about tomorrow's zoo trip. He flapped his hands, bounced on the bed and squealed until bedtime.
Saturday: he bounced in his seat the whole way there and shrieked at the elephants.
Sunday morning: when Lakshmi said, "No zoo today," Omkar burst into tears and lay face down on the floor.
"Next time," Lakshmi told her husband, "we'll tell him on the morning, not the night before."

qa.q: What did Omkar shriek at on Saturday?
qa.a: The elephants.

qa.q: What was Omkar feeling on Sunday when he burst into tears?
qa.a: He was disappointed and let down after two days of excitement, and may also have been tired from the trip.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi decide to change next time?
qa.a: To tell him about a trip only on the morning, so the build-up is smaller.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi's husband see the Sunday tears?
qa.a: He might see them as a strange overreaction until Lakshmi links them to the big build-up.

grounding: Over a weekend a toddler's bouncing, squealing excitement about the zoo turns to tears when it ends.

passage:
The kulfi cart's bell rang in the Kolkata lane. Saurabh flapped both hands and bounced, squealing, pulling at his uncle Deepak's kurta. Deepak laughed and bounced with him, and soon they were both hopping at the window.
The kulfi was cold and sweet. But when the last bit slid off the stick, Saurabh's face crumpled and he wailed.
Deepak scooped him up. "All gone. That was so exciting, and now it's finished. I know."

qa.q: What rang in the lane?
qa.a: The kulfi cart's bell.

qa.q: What was Saurabh feeling when the last bit slid off the stick?
qa.a: He was disappointed and sad that the treat was over, after all that excitement.

qa.q: What did Deepak do that helped when the tears came?
qa.a: He picked Saurabh up and named both the excitement and the ending, offering comfort.

qa.q: How did Deepak feel when Saurabh bounced at the window?
qa.a: Deepak caught the excitement and felt playful, bouncing along with him. 😊

grounding: A toddler's contagious excitement about a treat turns to tears when it ends, and his uncle comforts him.

passage:
"Nana's coming! Nana's coming!" Urmila squealed, bouncing at the window.
"She's been like this for an hour," said her mother.
"Don't wind her up more, Harsha," she warned her husband.
"Car! Car!" Harsha shouted, and Urmila shrieked, flapping her hands.
But when Nana walked in, Urmila hid behind the curtain and started to cry.
"Too much build-up," said her mother. Harsha picked her up gently. "It's okay. Nana will wait."

qa.q: Where did Urmila hide when Nana walked in?
qa.a: Behind the curtain.

qa.q: Why did Urmila cry when Nana finally arrived?
qa.a: After an hour of excitement she was probably overwhelmed, and the big moment tipped into tears.

qa.q: What could the family try next time a visitor is coming?
qa.a: Keep the build-up calmer and shorter, rather than winding her up for an hour.

qa.q: How might Nana feel when Urmila hides and cries?
qa.a: Nana might feel a little hurt, but understand that Urmila was overwhelmed.

grounding: A toddler bounces and squeals for an hour waiting for her grandfather, and the big build-up turns to tears.

passage:
Daycare note, Thursday, from Ayesha (room teacher)

To Farhan's mother: when I said "garden time", Farhan flapped his hands, bounced on his toes and squealed. Two other children started bouncing too! He ran round the slide again and again. When I called everyone in, he flopped on the grass and sobbed. I sat beside him and we waved goodbye to the slide together. After a drink of water he settled and joined story time. 🙂

qa.q: What did Farhan do when Ayesha said "garden time"?
qa.a: He flapped his hands, bounced on his toes and squealed.

qa.q: What was Farhan most likely feeling when he flopped on the grass and sobbed?
qa.a: Most likely disappointed that the fun was ending after such a big build-up of excitement. He may also have been hot or thirsty, since he settled after a drink of water.

qa.q: What small step could help Farhan when garden time ends another day?
qa.a: A warning a few minutes before, such as "two more turns, then goodbye slide", could make the ending feel less sudden.

qa.q: How are the other children affected by Farhan's excitement?
qa.a: His excitement spreads to them: two of them start bouncing too, so his joy lifts the whole group.

grounding: It shows a toddler's bodily, catching excitement before an outing and the tears that come when it ends.
